contexts: four acute hospitals, 12 medical and surgical wards
catheters inserted mostly in emergency and theatres
one Lean coach, one hospital at a time
paper catheter records in Hospital D
reading: Catheter duration is set by a chain of handoffs from the inserting team to the ward, where the indication is often lost and no one owns removal. Standard work at the ward (nurse-driven removal, huddle check, flowsheet reminder) acts at the point where waits accumulate. The single Lean coach forces a staggered start, which is also the design that gives the most power to separate change from secular trends. Hospital D's paper records and pending information governance agreement shape how its data can be measured and shared. Infections are the outcome patients care about most but are too few on 12 wards to show change.
